name: LA-01
label: Safe R

key_factors: Deep-red district with a Republican partisan lean of about 20 points
Steve Scalise is a well-funded, senior incumbent with a $10.6 million war chest
Democrat Lauren Jewett has raised only about $143,000 with minimal cash on hand
Prediction markets price Scalise at roughly 96% to win
model.rationale: Scalise holds a seat whose partisan lean is roughly 20 points Republican, has outraised his opponent by more than 70 to 1, and markets give him about a 96% chance of winning. With no polls or expert ratings suggesting any competitive threat, the fundamentals point to a comfortable Republican hold.
model.watch: A major national Democratic wave or an unexpected scandal could narrow the margin, but nothing in the current evidence suggests the seat is in play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Louisiana's 1st District is one of the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of about 20 points toward the GOP. Steve Scalise, the House Majority Leader and a senior incumbent, is seeking another term and holds an enormous financial advantage, having raised more than $10.6 million with $3.9 million still on hand.

Democrat Lauren Jewett has raised only about $143,000 and had under $12,000 in cash as of the latest filings, leaving her little capacity to compete in a district this favorable to Republicans. Prediction markets price Scalise at roughly 96%, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. The main question is the size of Scalise's winning margin, not who wins.
